question: When are SASSA payments made in 2026?
answer:

  • Old Age Grants: 2nd-3rd of each month
  • Disability Grants: 4th-5th of each month
  • Child Support Grants: Starting from the 6th of each month
  • Foster Care & Care Dependency Grants: Mid-month, typically 10th-15th

Key Tip: Always verify exact dates on the official SASSA website or at your local office, as holidays or technical issues may shift schedules. Stay informed with our payment calendar for real-time updates!

question: How do I apply for a SASSA grant in 2026?
answer:
Applying for a SASSA grant is straightforward but requires preparation. Follow these steps:

  1. Visit a SASSA office or outreach event – Locate one via our resources page.
  2. Gather documents:
    • South African ID
    • Proof of income (if any)
    • 3-month bank statements
    • Medical reports (for Disability Grant)
    • Child’s birth certificate (for Child Support or Foster Care Grants)
  3. Fill out the application form with SASSA staff assistance.
  4. Submit and get a receipt – Keep it safe!
  5. Wait for processing – Typically 30-90 days, depending on the grant type.

Online Option (for SRD Grant): Apply via srd.sassa.gov.za using your ID and mobile number.

Warning: SASSA applications are FREE. Avoid scams by applying only through official channels. Learn more about fraud prevention on our scams page.

question: Who qualifies for the SASSA Child Support Grant in 2026?
answer:
The Child Support Grant (CSG) supports caregivers raising children under 18. Here’s who qualifies:

For the Child:

  • Under 18 years old
  • South African citizen or permanent resident
  • Living in South Africa

For the Caregiver:

  • Primary caregiver (parent, guardian, or relative)
  • South African citizen or permanent resident
  • Meets income thresholds (means test)
  • Living in South Africa

2026 Income Thresholds:

  • Single caregiver: R5,500/month or less
  • Married/cohabiting: Combined income of R11,000/month or less

Grant Amount: R570/month per child (effective October 2026).

Tip: Apply early to avoid delays! Check eligibility details on our eligibility guide.

  • Affidavit for loss

  • Pay a small fee (if applicable)

  • Collect at your designated pay point

question: What does it mean when my SASSA application status says 'Pending', 'Approved', or 'Declined'?
answer:
Understanding your SASSA application status is crucial for knowing what to expect next:

Status Meanings:

  • Pending: Your application is under review. SASSA is verifying documents, income, or medical details (if applicable). This can take 7-120 days, depending on the grant type.
  • Approved: Your application meets eligibility criteria. Payments will start soon, typically within 30 days. You’ll receive a payment date and method confirmation.
  • Declined: Your application did not meet eligibility requirements (e.g., income too high, incomplete documents, or failed means test).

Next Steps:

  • Pending: Check status regularly via srd.sassa.gov.za (for SRD) or SMS to 34548 (R1). Ensure all documents are submitted to avoid delays.
  • Approved: Confirm payment method (bank, SASSA card, or paypoint). Collect your first payment as per the schedule.
  • Declined: Request a rejection letter from SASSA and appeal within 90 days with new evidence. See our appeals guide.

Tip: Save your reference number to track updates. Visit our status tracking guide for more.

  2. Ensure bank details are correct and linked to your ID.
  3. Contact SASSA at 0800 60 10 11 with your reference number.
  4. Resubmit missing documents if notified.

Processing Time: Typically 7-30 days, but can take longer during peak periods.

Tip: Regularly check your status and respond to SASSA queries. Visit our tracking guide.

question: What is the SASSA mandatory biometric system starting September 2026?
answer:
The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) will implement a mandatory Beneficiary Biometric Enrolment system from 1 September 2026 to enhance security and combat fraud. This system requires all new grant applicants to provide biometric data, such as fingerprints or facial recognition, through electronic Know Your Client (eKYC) technology. The initiative aims to verify beneficiary authenticity, reduce fraudulent applications, and ensure grants reach eligible recipients.

Key Features:

  • Fraud Prevention: Detects forged IDs and duplicate payments.
  • Proof of Life: Confirms beneficiaries are alive at application.
  • Streamlined Process: Simplifies documentation and improves audit outcomes.

Note: Only new applicants from September 2026 are required to enroll initially, but existing beneficiaries may need to comply later. Visit www.sassa.gov.za for updates or call 0800 60 1011. Learn more on our biometrics guide.

question: Who needs to complete the SASSA biometric enrolment in September 2026?
answer:
Starting 1 September 2026, the mandatory biometric enrolment applies to:

  • New Applicants: Anyone applying for a SASSA grant (e.g., Child Support, Disability, SRD) must provide fingerprints or facial recognition data.
  • Existing Beneficiaries Under Review: Those flagged for identity checks or updating personal details may need to enroll.
  • Alternative ID Users: Beneficiaries using non-standard IDs (e.g., quad 7 numbers) must comply, as per earlier SASSA policies from May 2026.

Exemption: Current beneficiaries not under review are not required to enroll immediately but may need to later. Bring your South African ID to a SASSA office for a quick scan. Check our biometrics guide or call 0800 60 1011 for clarification.

question: How do I complete the SASSA biometric enrolment process in 2026?
answer:
To complete the mandatory biometric enrolment starting 1 September 2026:

  1. Visit a SASSA Office: Go to your nearest SASSA branch or mobile unit.
  2. Bring Documents: Carry your South African ID (smart ID preferred), or alternative IDs like green ID book or Home Affairs receipts.
  3. Biometric Capture: Staff will scan your fingerprints or face using electronic Know Your Client (eKYC) technology. The process takes minutes.
  4. Receive Confirmation: Get a reference number to track your application.

Important: Applications without biometrics will be flagged for review, delaying payments. Visit www.sassa.gov.za or check our biometrics guide for office locations and tips.

question: What happens if I don’t complete the SASSA biometric enrolment in 2026?
answer:
If you fail to complete the mandatory biometric enrolment starting 1 September 2026:

  • New Applicants: Your grant application will be placed under review and not processed until biometrics are captured.
  • Existing Beneficiaries: If flagged for review (e.g., due to alternative IDs or suspicious activity), your grant may be suspended until you comply.
  • Deadline Risks: Missing deadlines, like the 22 June 2026 biometric update for some beneficiaries, could lead to permanent grant suspension.

Action: Visit a SASSA office with your ID to enroll. Check notifications via SMS or srd.sassa.gov.za. See our biometrics guide for details.

question: Will elderly SASSA beneficiaries need to provide biometrics in 2026?
answer:
Elderly SASSA beneficiaries (60+ years, receiving Old Age Grants) are not immediately required to provide biometrics unless they are:

  • New Applicants: Applying for a grant after 1 September 2026.
  • Flagged for Review: Due to alternative IDs, data updates, or suspected fraud.
  • Updating Details: Changing payment methods or personal information.

Concerns: Some elderly beneficiaries worry about unreadable fingerprints due to age. SASSA offers facial recognition as an alternative. For mobility issues, contact 0800 60 1011 to arrange assistance or mobile unit visits. Check our biometrics guide for support options.

question: How does the SASSA biometric system prevent fraud in 2026?
answer:
The SASSA biometric system, mandatory from 1 September 2026, prevents fraud by:

  • Verifying Identity: Fingerprints and facial recognition ensure applicants are authentic and alive.
  • Reducing Duplicates: Detects multiple applications using the same ID.
  • Stopping Forgery: Replaces unreliable green ID checks with secure eKYC technology.
  • Flagging Issues: Applications without biometrics are reviewed, preventing unauthorized payments.

Impact: SASSA reported 1,650 identity theft attempts in 2024 and R140 million paid to deceased beneficiaries, highlighting the need for this system. Learn more on our fraud prevention page or visit www.sassa.gov.za.

question: Is my biometric data safe with SASSA in 2026?

Concerns: Some experts warn of potential hacking risks. Report suspicious activity to SASSA at 0800 60 1011. Visit our privacy guide for tips on protecting your data.
